name: Urban Company Ltd

ar26.what: Annual report FY26 with notice of the 12th AGM (held 30-Jun-2026)

segments.ics: India Consumer Services (ex-InstaHelp): a managed marketplace for home services in 51 Indian cities: beauty and wellness (salon at home, spa), cleaning and pest control, electricians, plumbers, carpenters, appliance repair, painting (Revamp). Urban Company trains, equips and rates ~79,000 monthly active service partners and takes a commission plus fees; it also sells products and consumables to partners (B2B2C). NTV ₹3,167 cr in FY26 (74% of group).
segments.international: UAE (Dubai, Abu Dhabi) and Singapore, wholly owned and profitable since FY26; NTV ₹700 cr in FY26 (+75%). Saudi Arabia runs as Yammak, a 50:50 joint venture with SMASCO (listed manpower firm), equity-accounted (not in consolidated NTV or revenue).
segments.native: Native: own-brand water purifiers (RO, sold with a service plan) and electronic door locks, sold on the app, on Amazon/Flipkart and in shops; NTV ₹345 cr in FY26 (+122%), revenue ₹267 cr.
segments.instahelp: InstaHelp: on-demand, high-frequency house help (daily cleaning and housekeeping) booked by the hour; first orders in Q1FY26 (72,000), 3.82 million orders and NTV ₹53 cr in Q1FY27 at an average order of ₹138; adjusted EBITDA loss ₹132 cr in the quarter (₹346 per order). Competes with venture-funded Snabbit and Pronto.

guidanceAndCall.what: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3FY28 and ~₹1,000 cr of adjusted EBITDA by FY31 (reiterated in Q1FY27).
guidanceAndCall.src: Q4FY26 letter; Q1FY27 letter and call (CEO Abhiraj Singh Bhal)

guidanceAndCall.what: India Consumer Services: long-term (steady-state) adjusted EBITDA margin of 9-10% of NTV 'over the next few years'; Q1 is seasonally the strongest quarter for margins, so margins are best read annually. No NTV growth guidance.

InstaHelp: 'over the next 2 years, if not longer, will continue to take investments'; losses to stay elevated while it prioritises market leadership; category needs ~₹200 an hour pricing to break even (vs ~₹150 gross-margin breakeven); getting there could take 'a couple of years' or, in the worst case, five.
InstaHelp TAM in the top 15 cities: ₹7,000-12,000 cr of NTV (bull case ₹10,000-12,000 cr).
Native: line of sight of profitability over the next few quarters; target a ₹1,000 cr net-revenue business in the years to come.
International: UAE and Singapore to stay profitable while growth is maximised; KSA JV has line of sight of profitability in the coming quarters; no new international markets.
Middle East conflict: UAE demand fell ~15-20% in the last 3-4 weeks of Q4FY26; rupee depreciation and commodity prices to raise input costs for B2B2C products, Revamp panels and Native.
Capital allocation: once consolidated adjusted EBITDA breaks even ('latest in the next 18 months or so') management will revisit how to deploy the balance-sheet cash.

history: Incorporated in Dec-2014 by Abhiraj Singh Bhal, Varun Khaitan and Raghav Chandra as UrbanClap Technologies; later renamed Urban Company. Built a full-stack, managed model: it trains, equips, prices and rates its service partners.
Peak loss (₹514 cr); ₹1,383 cr of cash from financing (venture rounds) in the year (Screener cash-flow statement).
Losses cut from ₹312 cr to ₹93 cr; India Consumer Services adjusted EBITDA close to breakeven by FY24; Native water purifiers scale up.

First profit (₹240 cr), but only because of a ₹211 cr one-time deferred-tax credit; underlying PBT ₹29 cr. KSA moved into a 50:50 JV with SMASCO (deconsolidated from Jan-2025). InstaHelp launched (Mar-2025).

IPO at ₹103 (10-12 Sep 2025; listed 17-Sep-2025 at a 57% premium): ₹472 cr fresh issue, ₹1,428 cr offer for sale. InstaHelp scaled to 2.7 mn orders a quarter at a ₹235 cr full-year loss; group net loss ₹235 cr (incl. ₹60 cr deferred-tax reversal).
Q1FY27: group NTV +42%, core adjusted EBITDA ₹67 cr; InstaHelp loss ₹132 cr. SBI Mutual Fund became a >6% holder; venture investors kept selling after the Mar-2026 lock-in expiry.

sharesOutstanding.src: FY26 annual report: note 14 (146,21,80,603 shares outstanding net of 8,00,00,000 treasury shares held by the Urban Company ESOP Trust; founders' 9,77,62,500 shares = 6.34% of 154.22 cr issued) and note 32 (9,99,88,718 options outstanding at ₹1)

cash.src: Q1FY27 letter (cash & treasury investments by quarter); Screener balance sheet (cash ₹532 cr + investments ₹1,262 cr); the ₹227 cr difference is fixed deposits inside other assets

otherIncomeFY26.src: FY26 annual report, consolidated note 22 (other income)

accounting: Adjusted EBITDA (company definition) = PBT less other income, plus finance cost, D&A, ESOP cost, one-offs (listing expenses, a ₹9 cr warehouse fire loss in Q1FY26) and the KSA JV loss, LESS lease payments: rent is treated as an operating cost. Ind AS EBITDA adds rent back (₹38 cr in FY26).
Screener's operating profit includes the share of the KSA JV loss (₹31 cr FY26), so its FY26 EBITDA (−₹254 cr) is ₹31 cr below the company's Ind AS EBITDA (−₹223 cr).

FY25 profit (₹240 cr) included a one-time deferred-tax credit of ₹211 cr; FY26 includes a ₹60 cr reversal of deferred-tax assets (losses likely to lapse as InstaHelp scales, and ESOP exercises). DTA of ₹151.5 cr remains on the balance sheet at Mar-26 (standalone).
ESOP: 10.0 cr options outstanding at Mar-26 at ₹1 (6.1 cr exercisable), settled through an ESOP trust that holds 8.0 cr treasury shares. ESOP expense ₹104 cr in FY26, ₹38 cr in Q1FY27.
Contingent liabilities ₹116 cr (mainly GST demands under dispute; ₹52 cr paid under protest).
Auditor rotation: Price Waterhouse & Co (term completed) replaced by BSR & Co. LLP from the 2026 AGM; no qualification in the FY26 audit report.
management: Co-founder, Chairperson, MD & CEO (promoter; 6.34% at Mar-26)
